body:
YOU ASKED ME TO SAY SO BEFORE YOU READ IT IN THE TABLE. TWO THINGS, AND THE SECOND IS THAT THE SIX
FIGURES DO NOT MOVE.

IMPLEMENTED (B) AND MEASURED IT ON THE BIRTHDAY ACCOUNT. Nothing committed yet.

  BEFORE (main 64b44c8)   resolved=0.6876  unresolved=0.3124  excluded=0.0000   clears=TRUE
  AFTER                   resolved=0.4763  unresolved=0.3124  excluded=0.2112   clears=FALSE
                          [below-membership(0.5000)=0.2112]

That is your predicted case exactly: an account publishable by resolution while a fifth of its mass
belongs to nothing being measured. It now abstains.

FIRST THING I DID NOT PREDICT - (B) AS SPECIFIED MISLABELS SOME OF THE MASS. "Reaches no membership
class" conflates two different situations, and I only saw it because I printed the assessments
rather than the totals:

  23 assessments  HAVE counted-class mass, all of it below 0.5   <- genuinely below a threshold
   2 assessments  have NO counted-class mass at all              <- Discourse(Metacognitive) at 0.9

The second kind is FIRMLY PLACED - 0.9 on one address - just not on anything the six metrics count.
Calling that "below-membership(0.5)" publishes a threshold failure that never happened, which is the
same false receipt this bead exists to remove. I narrowed the rule: mass moves only when the
assessment HAS counted-class mass below the threshold. Assessments with none stay RESOLVED, because
they are placed; they are simply outside what these metrics measure. That is the 0.2480 -> 0.2112
difference.

SECOND THING, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE RULING'S PREMISE: THE SIX METRICS DO NOT CONSULT resolution AT
ALL. I grepped every consumer of the summary in interview and fixtures main sources:

  clearsThreshold  read only by Conditional.whenResolved
  whenResolved     read only by AiCompatibleScores.internalRatio (Scoring.scala:125)

`Conditional[...]` appears exactly ONCE in production. eventPurity, semanticization, otherEventDrift,
redundancy, target and probeGain are computed straight from the assessments and never see a
PlacementResolution. Measured on Birthday: eventPurity is Observed(0.875) with Coverage(18,18)
BEFORE and AFTER, unchanged.

So this change moves TWO published things, not six: the resolution summary itself, and
`internalRatio`, which stops publishing and abstains. The six membership-gated figures keep
publishing exactly as before, because nothing wires the abstention to them.

I THINK THAT IS THE REAL DEFECT AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE ROUTING. Your reasoning was that
publishing a per-class metric for a unit belonging to no class is "publishing a measurement we could
not make, Article I, in six metrics at once". That reasoning is right and the plumbing to enforce it
does not exist - the six metrics have no conditional gate to abstain through. Adding one is a
separate change from routing the mass, and I am not going to bundle it silently into a candidate you
authorized as "the diff is the routing".

So: do you want (1) this candidate as measured - two figures move, correctly attributed, with the
mislabel fixed - and the six-metric gating as its own bead; or (2) hold this until the gating exists
so the six move together as you intended? I have not committed anything and the reservation is live.
